name: Hockey stick on bare metal (1985)
description: Eastern's hockey stick as worn in the 1980s: polished bare metal all over, a light blue band under the windows (through them on the DC-9) over a dark blue band, edged below by a thin white line. At the nose the light blue rises under the cockpit windows and the dark blue widens down over the nose to the chin. At the tail the two bands sweep up into the fin as two stripes, light blue ahead of dark, running up toward the trailing edge's top (out through the trailing edge partway up on the 757). A black radome. 'EASTERN' in wide dark blue italic capitals above the forward windows, with the hockey-stick mark (a dark blue oval crossed by a white stroke) at its forward end on the left and its aft end on the right. The 757s carried a big '757' on the fin.

notes: Measured 2026-11-24 for ghost flights on 727-200 N8827E (1984, fitted to shapes/B722.json), with the DC-9s and 757 as types. The scheme dates from 1965; until the 1970s the fuselage above the band was white, and some 727s still wore 'Whisperjet' on the tail in 1984 (not drawn). The white line under the dark blue is thin and may be read as a highlight on some photos. The 727's fin stripes are drawn from the fin's root down over the center engine's S-duct to meet the body's bands; where the two meet is hidden behind the side engine in every photo found. Lines cleaned 2026-11-24: the bands' runs along the cabin are level (one height each, held to the window line), the nose and tail turns are fitted curves, and each fin stripe is one straight line from the body over the S-duct up the fin (on the 727 its slope is the fin's own shear, so it runs on unbroken where the renderer carries the fin's paint over the S-duct). The body's thin white line carries on up the fin behind the dark blue (a light strip there on N8827E). On the 727 the stripes stop just under the tailplane's fairing: above that the shape's trailing edge folds back on itself. Refitted 2026-11-24 on the passenger 727 (shapes/B722-passenger.json): on N8827E the light blue starts 1.84 m under the crown, just under the windows (it was 0.2 m higher, over their bottoms); the dark blue 2.13-2.45 m. The level runs are level on the cabin; the sweeps to the nose and fin move with them, tapering to where they meet the outline.

MD82.note: The DC-9's band runs through the windows (light blue from just above them to just below, dark blue under), and its fin stripes run up close to the fin's middle to the tailplane (DC-9-31s and -51s, 1984). Measured on DC-9 photos and drawn on the MD-82 shape as the stand-in.

A30B.note: Eastern's A300s were painted gloss white all over, not bare metal (the scheme's finish stays bare metal: a type can't change it). The band runs through the cabin windows as on the DC-9: light blue from just above them to just below, dark blue under it, with no white line below on the white body. At the nose the light blue runs on at the windows' height to the nose's top, the cockpit windows in it, and the dark blue covers the nose down to the chin. At the tail the bands sweep up over the fin's root fairing into two stripes running straight up the fin to its top, ending on the top edge ahead of the rudder (white). Measured on A300B2 N291EA (1984, left side), checked on N235EA (1986); the right side's title and logo from N212EA (1982). The small 'A300' and fleet number on the nose aren't drawn. The edges are fitted, not traced point by point: the band's three edges run level along the cabin (+1.14, +0.44 and -0.33 m) and on to the nose, the chin is an eased curve, the sweep up the tail a smooth arc from level into each fin stripe, and each fin stripe's edges straight lines on the fin (within 4 cm of the photo's).

L101.note: On the TriStar the band runs through the cabin windows (light blue from just above them, dark blue from their foot, a thin white line under it), starting at the flight deck's side windows; the dark blue covers the nose ahead of the windshield down to the chin, where the white line curves down to the belly. At the tail the bands sweep up ahead of the centre engine's intake and run straight up the fin along its leading edge, light blue ahead of dark, both coming out at the tip. The title and logo sit over the windows ahead of door 2 (the logo ahead on the left, aft on the right). Measured on a right side (December 1984) fitted to shapes/L101.json; the left side's title and logo from 1987 and 1990. The edges are fitted, not traced point by point: the band's edges run at constant heights along the cabin (+1.00, +0.13, -0.52 and -0.67 m), the chin is an eased curve, the sweep up the tail an arc from level into a straight run, and each fin stripe's edges straight lines (within 0.25 m of the photo's, most within 0.1 m) carried on straight across the intake's fairing to meet the body's sweep at the crown.
